neighbours.label: attributive 'loose' (and to a lesser degree 'tight') directly modifying a noun ('loose tongue', 'loose policy', 'loose tea'); predicative 'is loose / broke loose' stays quiet
fire: Critics blamed the crash on the central bank's loose lending rules.
The editor cut a few loose threads from the final chapter.
My grandmother always buys loose leaf tea from the market.
He lost the job because of his loose talk at the party.
The doctor checked the child for loose joints and weak muscles.
Wear loose clothing when you visit the temple in summer.
The detective followed every loose end in the case.
Managers worry about the tight budget for next year.
quiet: Critics blamed the crash on the central bank, whose rules were too lenient.
The editor cut a few threads that were left hanging in the final chapter.
My grandmother always buys tea in bags from the market.
He lost the job because of his careless talk at the party.
The doctor checked whether the child's joints felt stable.
Wear light clothing when you visit the temple in summer.
The detective noticed a screw had come loose in the lock.
Managers worry about the small budget for next year.

notes: Probe: attributive loose 0.36-0.69, tight deadline 0.34; predicative 'is loose', 'broke loose', 'hung loose', 'let loose' 0.02-0.07. Near misses use loose predicatively or swap a synonym.
